title: Collection is getting deleted automatically from qdrant vector db in production environment.
body:
The created collection in the qdrant is getting deleted automatically. 

Currently , I have hosted the qdrant  instance in GCP and the collections are getting deleted automatically .But the collections in qdrant in local host environment its seems to be fine and doesnt face the issue.

**Qdrant server version : v1.7.3**

**GCP Resources:**
1.Memory 32GiB
2.CPU 8

This is the code I am using to create the collection:

```
def create_collection(collection_name):
    url = f'{qdrant_url}/collections/{collection_name}'
    headers = {
        'Authorization': f'Bearer {qdrant_api_key}',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
    payload = {"vectors": {"size": 1536, "distance": "Cosine"}}
    response = requests.put(url, json=payload, headers=headers)

    if response.status_code == 200:
        print("Collection created successfully")
    else:
        print(f"Error: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Your creation request looks fine. Qdrant never deletes a collection on its own.

Are you sure your instance has storage properly configured? In other words, are you sure that if your Docker container restarts all data is properly kept?

By the way, since you're using Python we recommend to use our Python client instead: https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant-client

comments.body: Even I've got the same issue but locally, the data does persistent on the local volume that's been mounted. A volume mount is all I'm using and I've noticed that a container restart, doesn't have any issues. It's only after a docker restart have I noticed a data loss.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant1 Im running Docker and the rest on a M2 Mac, do let me know if any other details would help you. I haven't had this issue with any other containers like MongoDB, etc. 

Im using a docker-compse file at the moment 

```yaml
version: 3.1
services:
    image: qdrant/qdrant
    restart: always
    volumes:
        - ./data:/qdrant/storage
    ports:
        - 6333:6333
        - 6334:6334
```

Now that I look at this, i feel like maybe I might have messed up the volume mounting. Do advise.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
First of all, it looks like you're missing a service name in there. You might want to have this:

```
version: 3.1
services:
    qdrant:
            image: qdrant/qdrant
            restart: always
            volumes:
                - ./data:/qdrant/storage
            ports:
                - 6333:6333
                - 6334:6334
```

I see that you store at `./data`. Since macOS runs Docker in a Linux VM, I'm not sure where it puts this data directory. Could you try mounting it to some absolute path. For example, a similar path to what you use for MongoDB?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant5 Could you check whether your collections survive:
1. restarting the Qdrant container
2. restarting your script to upload/search in Qdrant

If point 1 fails, you didn't set up mounts correctly. If so, please feel free to share how you set the container up.
If point 2 fails, you might accidentally be deleting the collection on start. That can be due to a `recreate_collection` call.
